resources.string: OnPath shows your map offline, plans your route and guides you on the way. For the dot on the map and the guidance it needs a few things from your phone. It takes about a minute – or do it later, when you start a tour.
OnPath can show where you are, record your tour and guide you.
You can set the rest up any time in Settings → Phone setup.
A tour needs your precise location. You can still plan and look at the map.
Your phone removed this because OnPath was not used for some months. That is normal – set it up again here.
This was switched off since you last used OnPath.
The dot on the map shows where you are. On a tour OnPath records your track and tells you about every turn. Your exact position and your tracks stay on your phone.
On the next screen, allow OnPath while you use the app – with precise location.
No problem – the map and planning work without it. For the dot on the map and a tour OnPath needs your location.
Android does not ask again. Tap Continue, then Permissions → Location, and allow it while using the app, with precise location.
Only with your exact position does OnPath record a clean track and buzz at the right junction. An approximate position can be a kilometre or more off – with it a tour cannot start.
On the next screen, change to precise location.

The Location switch on your phone (swipe down from the top of the screen) must be on, so OnPath can find you – for the dot on the map, your track and the turn buzzes. When it is off, no app knows where you are.
Tap Continue and switch location on.

On the lock screen OnPath shows the next turn, the time left and your arrival (“Left in 300 m · arrive 13:00”). If you leave the route while the phone is locked, OnPath asks there “New route?”. And if something goes wrong, like storage full, you hear about it at once. Turn vibration and recording work without it too.
Tap Continue and switch notifications for OnPath on.

With the phone in your pocket OnPath buzzes before junctions where you could go wrong: one buzz = left, two = right. Three long buzzes mean you have left the route. Some phones mute this – the test shows whether you feel it.
Hold the phone in your hand and tap Test.
Did you feel one buzz, then two?

Then your phone's vibration is turned down or off. On Pixel phones: Settings → Sound & vibration → Vibration & haptics → switch on Alarm vibration. On other phones look for vibration under Sound. Then test again.
This phone cannot vibrate. OnPath shows each turn on the screen and on the lock screen instead (“Left in 300 m”) – so keep notifications on.

With the screen off in your pocket, OnPath keeps recording your track and buzzes at turns. If your phone restricts OnPath's battery use, it can stop OnPath on the way – your track gets gaps and the buzzes stop.
Tap Continue, then Battery (or App battery usage), and choose Unrestricted or Optimized – not Restricted.

Phones from %1$s close apps in the background to save battery – sometimes in the middle of a tour, with the screen off. Recording then stops until you open OnPath again, and the turn buzzes stop too. A few settings on the phone prevent that.

1. Settings → Battery (on older phones: Battery and device care → Battery) → Background usage limits: switch off “Put unused apps to sleep”.
2. Tap “Never sleeping apps” → + and add OnPath. It must not be under “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
3. Tap “Open app settings” → Battery → “Unrestricted”.
The names can differ a little on your phone.

1. Tap “Open app settings” → “Autostart”: on.
2. In the same place: Battery saver → “No restrictions”.
3. Open the recent apps, hold OnPath (or pull it down) and tap the lock 🔒.
The names can differ a little on your phone.

1. Settings → Battery → “App launch” → OnPath: switch off “Manage automatically”.\n2. In the window that opens, switch on all three: “Auto-launch”, “Secondary launch”, “Run in background”.\nThe names can differ a little on your phone.

1. Tap “Open app settings” → Battery → “Don't optimize” (or “Allow background activity”).
2. Open the recent apps, hold OnPath and tap the lock 🔒.
3. If OnPath still stops on the way: Settings → Battery → Battery optimization → ⋮ → switch off “Advanced optimization”.
The names can differ a little on your phone.
Battery saver is on, and on this phone it switches GPS off as soon as the screen goes off. With the phone in your pocket your track would get gaps, and the turn buzzes would stop.
Battery saver is on, but on this phone it keeps GPS running with the screen off – your track stays complete.
Turn battery saver off for the tour – or keep the screen on.
When you don't use OnPath for a while

If you don't open OnPath for a few months, say over winter, Android takes back what you allowed it, like your location. At the first tour of the season OnPath then asks again – a few taps. With this switched off, everything simply keeps working after the break.
Tap Continue and switch off the setting for unused apps (on Pixel: “Pause app activity if unused”).
On – after a long break OnPath asks again
With these settings OnPath finds you, records your whole tour and guides you with the phone in your pocket. Tap a line to set it up.
